blocks.content: A FailedScheduling event means the scheduler's filtering stage, covered in the Internals module, eliminated every single node in the cluster, leaving nowhere at all for the Pod to actually go.

As covered in the Scheduler Workflow topic, filtering eliminates nodes that genuinely cannot run a given Pod, this failure mode is exactly what happens when filtering eliminates every single node, leaving none as viable candidates at all.

blocks.alt: The exact filtering stage covered in the Internals module, now taken to its failure extreme

blocks.content: If literally no node survives filtering, there is nothing left for the scoring or binding stages to even consider, scheduling fails outright, and the Pod remains stuck Pending, covered in its own topic in this module.

blocks.alt: Nothing left to even score or bind, scheduling simply cannot proceed

blocks.content: The most frequent real cause, no node in the entire cluster currently has enough free CPU or memory to satisfy the Pod's resource requests, covered in the Namespaces & Resource Management module.

blocks.alt: Not one node, every node, lacking the capacity this Pod actually needs

blocks.content: An overly restrictive nodeSelector or affinity rule, covered in the Scheduling module, that simply does not match any node currently in the cluster, is another frequent, real cause worth checking directly.

blocks.alt: A constraint that, correctly, matches absolutely nothing currently available

blocks.content: 5. Always Check the Event Message First
blocks.text: 5. Always Check the Event Message First

blocks.content: Rather than guessing among these possibilities, the actual FailedScheduling event message names the exact reason directly, "insufficient memory," "node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate," and similar, always the fastest path to the real answer.

blocks.alt: The exact reason, stated directly, always the fastest path to an answer

blocks.content:
kubectl describe pod my-app
# Warning  FailedScheduling  default-scheduler
# 0/5 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory, 2 node(s) had untolerated taint

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: FailedScheduling means the filtering stage eliminated every node, insufficient cluster-wide resources and unmatched affinity/taint rules are the most common real causes.
The event message always names the exact reason directly, check it first before guessing among the possible causes.
